Ten tsconfig files drop the two options TypeScript 7 removes — KS-2177 (KS-1398 step one, lane L5), a form change that also works on TypeScript 5

+
What to know. TypeScript 7 removes moduleResolution: node and baseUrl. Five tsconfig.json files (packages/shared, services/billing, nft-certificate, services/shared, wallet-connector; all module: commonjs) lose the moduleResolution line, because under commonjs TypeScript 5 resolves the same way without it. Five files (frontend admin, issuer, verifier, mobile/secuura-app, services/vc-issuer) lose baseUrl and every paths value that was not relative gains a ./. Neither node16 nor bundler is used: both fail for a commonjs file (TS5110, TS5095) and would need a module change. No TypeScript version, manifest or lock moves. +
Proof: on TypeScript 5.9.3, before and after the edit, the nine measured packages give equal tsc --noEmit results and equal sorted --listFiles (9 of 9 each); the emitted trees of the six emitting packages are byte for byte equal (638 of 638 files); the three frontends’ dist/ trees are byte for byte equal (90 of 90 files; two runs of the unedited tree are also identical, so the comparison could fail); the type-check ratchet reads 0 new and 0 stale in all five services, before and after; unit-test counts are equal before and after in all seven packages run. +
+
+
Not measured here. The mobile app (nothing installed there: its paths edit is a form change, not a proven cure), the frontends’ Docker image builds, the four platform suites, and TypeScript 7 for the other packages and for the frontends’ tests. TypeScript 7.0.2 was run in a scratch copy only: services/billing is still red there for TS6059 (a rootDir rule, not a removed option), which the version flip has to decide. +
+

@@ -0,0 +1,29 @@ +

. KS-2177 (KS-1398 step one, lane L5): ten tsconfig files drop moduleResolution: node and baseUrl, the two options TypeScript 7 removes (a form change that also works on TypeScript 5)

+
What this changes. Under Blockchain/Dev, five tsconfig.json files (packages/shared, services/billing, services/nft-certificate, services/shared, services/wallet-connector) lose their "moduleResolution": "node" line and five (frontend/admin, frontend/issuer, frontend/verifier, mobile/secuura-app, services/vc-issuer) lose "baseUrl": ".". (1) The five moduleResolution files are module: commonjs; with the line deleted TypeScript 5 resolves them as node10, which is what node meant. (2) Deleting baseUrl and leaving a non-relative paths value fails with TS5090, so each of those files also prefixes the value with ./: vendor/shared/src/* in the three frontends, eight src/... values in mobile, two node_modules/@secuura/shared/dist/... values in vc-issuer. paths then resolves from the tsconfig’s own directory, which is what baseUrl: "." was. The earlier lane text said node16 or bundler; neither compiles for a commonjs file (TS5110, TS5095, reproduced on tsc 5.9.3) and either would need a module change, which changes emit. +
This is a form change, not a proven cure. It proves TypeScript 5 sees the same program before and after; it does not prove the TypeScript 7 flip. One thing baseUrl did that paths does not is resolve a bare import such as from 'src/x' from the package root; a git grep at 1247e1af3c20 finds 0 such imports in the five packages (the alias form from '@/ finds 133 in admin), and a planted bare import compiles with baseUrl and fails without it, so the check can fail. Services whose tsconfig.json changed, for the A2 builder who adds tsconfig.test.json files: billing, wallet-connector (the line only) and vc-issuer (baseUrl and the paths prefix; its tsconfig.test.json extends it). +
+

.1 Equal before and after, on TypeScript 5.9.3

+
How each cell proves itself. By comparison that can fail: tsc --noEmit exit code and diagnostics equal and sorted --listFiles equal in 9 of 9 packages; the six emitting packages’ trees written to a scratch --outDir byte for byte equal (638 of 638 files); the three frontends’ dist/ byte for byte equal (90 of 90 files), with two runs of the unedited tree identical, so vite is deterministic here. The planted controls fired: one byte changed in a copy of an emitted file is reported (363 of 364 equal), and one planted type error in a scratch copy of a vc-issuer test file turns check.cjs red (rc 1, two new errors), then the file is restored (sha256 equal) and it is green again. +
The ratchet. npm run check:test-types reads 0 new and 0 stale before and after in auth (41 baseline errors), api-gateway (25), vc-issuer, security and m365-integration (0 each); no baseline file changed. The six emitting packages and api-gateway, auth and referral build with rc 0 before and after. +
Unit tests, before = after. The counts in the figures below are equal in all seven packages run; the two reds (wallet-signature in shared, two test files in frontend/issuer) were red before the edit. +
+

.2 TypeScript 7.0.2 in a scratch copy

+
A measurement, not a gate. Before the edit, TypeScript 7.0.2 refuses all nine configs on the removed options (TS5108 on the five moduleResolution files; TS5090 and TS5102 on the five baseUrl files). After it, 8 of 9 main configs read rc 0 with 0 errors. services/billing still reads rc 1 with TS6059: its include reaches ../../shared/types, outside the inferred rootDir; that is a rootDir decision for the version flip, not one of the two options here. With the six services’ test files included, no run shows a missing-global error (TS2304, TS2582, TS2593, TS2688), so no types array is added; the errors that do appear (TS1378, TS1343, TS6133 and a few others) are codes TypeScript 5.9.3 reports on the same files, plus one more TS6059 in billing. +

.4 What this does not prove

+
What was not driven. The mobile app: nothing is installed in mobile/secuura-app, so neither tsc nor its tests ran; its paths edit is a form change, and Expo 54.0.31’s base config and @expo/cli 54.0.21’s Metro resolver were read from the registry packages, not run. The frontends’ Docker image builds (they build vendor/shared), the four platform suites, TypeScript 7 on the frontends’ test files and on the other 35 packages, and services/billing’s TS6059 are not covered. +
